bug_semantics: Ech0 globally installed its i18n middleware and passed unauthenticated request-controlled locale values, including the raw Accept-Language header after only TrimSpace, to go-i18n and golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage without a size or shape bound. The x/text CVE-2022-32149 mitigation counted '-' separators but the parser also aliases '_' to '-', so a near-1 MiB malformed underscore-separated value bypassed the guard and exercised quadratic parsing, allowing unauthenticated CPU denial of service on every route. X-Locale and the lang query parameter also reached the same unbounded parser through ResolveLocale.
flaw_origin: Commit b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516 first created Ech0's complete remotely reachable vulnerable path: it added internal/i18n/i18n.go, forwarded unbounded locale values to ParseAcceptLanguage and goi18n.NewLocalizer, read Accept-Language from the request, and registered the middleware globally. The parser weakness pre-existed in x/text, but the immediate parent did not contain Ech0's i18n parser path or global exposure.

evidence: The assigned advisory describes Ech0 before 5.0.1 accepting an unbounded Accept-Language value in globally executed i18n middleware, the underscore alias bypass of x/text's separator guard, quadratic parsing, and unauthenticated CPU denial of service.

`git grep -n -E 'Accept-Language|NewLocalizer\(bundle|i18nUtil.Middleware' b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516 -- internal/i18n/i18n.go internal/router/middleware.go` shows the unfiltered NewLocalizer sink at i18n.go:65, the request header read at i18n.go:116, the additional ResolveLocale path at i18n.go:130, and global middleware registration at middleware.go:16. Pickaxe history for each of the header read, NewLocalizer sink, and registration traces their first application-history addition to b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516; later dc03197eeb4b5f28ebe794f45732cd4d04d53b1c preserves or rearranges the path rather than originating it.

`git cat-file -p b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516` shows one parent, b00c0f7da80cdbf4f4bd84a0c557ae03c88775a6. The direct diff creates internal/i18n/i18n.go as a new file and adds the router registration; it is not a merge, move, import, revert, release aggregate, or decomposable squash, so the ordinary commit is the smallest public-history BIC.

`git ls-tree -r --name-only b00c0f7da80cdbf4f4bd84a0c557ae03c88775a6 -- internal/i18n/i18n.go internal/router/middleware.go go.mod` lists only the pre-existing router middleware and go.mod, not internal/i18n/i18n.go. `git show b00c0f7da80cdbf4f4bd84a0c557ae03c88775a6:internal/router/middleware.go` shows only Recovery, Cors, and WriteGuard registration. Thus the vulnerable parser path and its global exposure are absent from the direct parent.

The introduction boundary is repository-verifiable: v4.0.0 resolves to 93b935c5b64020c7475abb9df071fdf8663b9f84 and has no matching i18n mechanism, while v4.1.0 resolves to d1f0768e8d469179d5ee8634c2c3311ed31e1d26 and contains the unfiltered NewLocalizer call, raw Accept-Language reads, and global middleware registration.

`git show a5e77c4af60ead1cad3b3e8e0a3ed6f30892ed09 -- internal/i18n/i18n.go` adds sanitizeAcceptLanguage and applies it to each ResolveLocale part and immediately before NewLocalizer, directly bounding both parser sinks. v5.0.0 resolves to 4deb936608843fab40692788cf299700bb6637bf and still has the raw unfiltered path; the clone has no v5.0.1 tag; v5.0.2 resolves to f715214732db93067718150cb3b2bad8fe9be827, contains the sanitizer at both sinks, and is the first repository-verifiable fixed tag containing the fix commit.
